company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS at $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the quality was low — the upside was driven by tariff refunds (145bp gross margin tailwind) and a non-cash LIFO benefit (105bp tailwind), not organic strength. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100bp year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence in fiscal 2027 growth.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex deeper into the robotics and AI-driven machine vision space.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid FQ1 EPS beat at 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat held up even excluding tariff refund tailwinds — adjusted EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. Sales disappointed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. For fiscal 2027, the sales guidance range was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS range of $1.85–2.15 was left unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings strong large-cap industrial CFO experience, having previously served in the role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International.

THOR missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% — well below the Street's 13.85% estimate — while management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure squeezing household budgets. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, down 8.4%, though slightly above the Street's $2.17 billion. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost-reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The result is a significant clinical milestone that reinforces Viking's position as a credible competitor in the high-stakes obesity drug market.

sectors: RV industry facing headwinds from elevated interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation per THOR's commentary, with retail demand remaining soft. GLP-1/obesity drug space getting a lift from VKTX's positive trial data. Robotics and Physical AI theme reinforced by CGNX's RealSense acquisition.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, with no broad macro or rates commentary included in today's dispatch. Let's run through the key names.

Starting with AutoZone — they beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but don't get too excited about the quality here. The upside was almost entirely driven by tariff refunds, a 145 basis point gross margin tailwind, and a non-cash LIFO benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture gets less impressive fast. Domestic comps missed at plus 1.6% versus the Street's plus 3.1%, and operating expenses as a percent of sales rose 100 basis points year over year. Management did note that sales linearity improved in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027, but this was a low-quality beat. Mixed read on the stock.

Cognex is buying RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. RealSense is expected to do $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year over year. This is a bullish strategic move, doubling down on the robotics and AI-driven machine vision theme that's been a major market narrative.

MillerKnoll delivered a genuine earnings beat — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents — and importantly the beat holds up even after backing out tariff refunds, which were an 11-cent tailwind. Adjusted that's 42 cents, still well above consensus. Sales missed at $923 million versus the Street's $943 million, but orders rose 3.5% year over year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly while EPS guidance was left unchanged. Call it mixed but leaning positive on execution.

THOR Industries missed on fiscal fourth quarter EPS at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year over year to 12.4%. Management's tone was cautious — calling out stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets. Revenue did come in slightly above estimates at $2.3 billion, and there were some bright spots: dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost cuts are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year over year. Still, this is a bearish print overall.

Viking Therapeutics is the big pre-market mover — shares spiking after reporting positive trial results for VK2735, their GLP-1 obesity drug, showing 22% weight loss. That's a major clinical milestone and keeps Viking firmly in the conversation as a serious competitor in the obesity space. Clearly bullish.

Finally, Pentair named a new CFO — Bob Hau, starting November 1st, with a strong track record including prior CFO roles at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Largely a housekeeping item but worth noting for a name.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the standout momentum story, Cognex has a strategic catalyst with the RealSense deal, AutoZone's beat won't inspire much confidence given the quality, and THOR remains under macro pressure. Stay focused and trade the tape.
